units.statement: TRIM is a multimodal conditional variational autoencoder with separate RNA and TCR encoders, shared latent space, separate decoders, contrastive clonality loss, and learned condition embeddings (patient, source, timepoint) enabling joint reconstruction and cross-modal generation.
source_quotes: The encoders and decoders are trained jointly under a variational autoencoder regime.

units.statement: TRIM predicts intra-tumor and post-treatment T cell clonal expansion and transcriptional status from pre-treatment blood-derived paired RNA+TCR data, outperforming RNA-only or TCR-only baselines and capturing faithful TCR repertoire diversity (Shannon entropy, clone size distributions) across held-out patients and conditions.
source_quotes: By explicitly modeling clonal identity and expansion dy- namics, TRIM enables predictions that go beyond label classification to generate full gene expression profiles and clonal behaviors for unseen cells at later time points or different tissue sites, overcoming the limitations of previous methods and unlocking new applications in immunological inference.

In all settings, TRIM accurately predicted intra-tumor T cell clonal expansion and transcriptional status based on T cells from blood or normal tissue before treatment, demonstrating its utility in modeling multimodal T cell data and predicting T cell response to treatment and disease progression.
